content: Croflemer has been observed to increase the levels of conjugated estrogens in the vaginal environment by influencing the metabolism of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. This interaction necessitates close monitoring and caution during use. Crofelemer has the potential to inhibit CYP3A4, as well as transporters MRP2 and OATP1A2, at concentrations expected in the gastrointestinal tract. However, due to its minimal systemic absorption, it is unlikely to exert systemic inhibition. Similarly, crofelemer increases the levels of crizotinib, cyclophosphamide, cyclosporine, dantrolene, dapsone, darifenacin, darunavir, dasatinib, dexamethasone, diazepam, disopyramide, dronedarone, efavirenz, eletriptan, elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF, eplerenone, ergoloid mesylates, ergotamine, erlotinib, erythromycin base, erythromycin ethylsuccinate, erythromycin stearate, esomeprazole, estradiol, synthetic conjugated estrogens, estropipate, eszopiclone, ethosuximide, etoposide, etravirine, exemestane, felbamate, felodipine, fenofibrate, fexofenadine, finerenone, flibanserin, flurazepam, flutamide, fosamprenavir, fosaprepitant, haloperidol, imatinib, indinavir, isavuconazonium sulfate, isosorbide dinitrate, isosorbide mononitrate, isradipine, ivacaftor, and lapatinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. These interactions require careful monitoring and, in some cases, therapy modification. For certain drugs, such as finerenone, serum potassium levels should be monitored during initiation and dosage adjustments, as crofelemer may increase the risk of adverse effects when co-administered with weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Similarly, co-administration with flibanserin may lead to increased adverse effects, particularly when combined with multiple weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. In all cases, the potential for crofelemer to inhibit CYP3A4 and transporters MRP2 and OATP1A2 in the gut should be considered, although systemic inhibition is unlikely due to its minimal absorption. Close monitoring and appropriate adjustments to therapy are recommended to mitigate potential drug interactions and ensure patient safety.
